questions.q: What is the point of listing every layer of Project 1 with its specific source lesson, as this wrap-up does?
options: It shows the project drew on named techniques from every course in the track as one coherent system, not as separate disconnected exercises
It's a formatting requirement with no bearing on understanding the build
Only the ingestion layer actually used techniques from prior lessons
The citations are decorative and could be removed without changing the retrospective's value
questions.explain: Databricks & Delta Lake, Fabric & Real-Time Analytics, and this course's own Chapter 1 all show up together in one build.

questions.q: According to the retrospective, what specifically would need to change first if online-order volume grew 10x?
options: A single Eventstream may not keep up, and Databricks' OPTIMIZE/ZORDER BY on FactSales becomes necessary rather than optional
The entire star schema would need to be redesigned from scratch
Nothing would need to change — the design scales indefinitely as built
The dashboard's visual layout would need to change
questions.explain: The lesson names the Eventstream's throughput and FactSales's file organization as the specific bottlenecks at 10x online-order volume.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say idempotent MERGE ingestion "made the hardening strategy actually safe, not a hand-wave"?
options: Because retries during hardening only work safely if re-running the same operation produces the same result, which is exactly what the idempotent MERGE from ingestion guarantees
Idempotency and retry safety are unrelated concepts
MERGE statements are always unsafe to retry regardless of idempotency
The hardening lesson replaced the idempotent MERGE with a different mechanism
questions.explain: This connects Lesson 65's ingestion design directly to Lesson 68's hardening strategy — one decision enabling the other.

questions.q: What skill is this retrospective lesson explicitly practicing, per its reference to Lesson 24?
options: Explaining a finished system design out loud, under interview-style pressure, including what would change at scale
Writing unit tests for the pipeline's PySpark transformations
Memorizing every lesson number in the track
Designing a brand-new system from a blank requirements document
questions.explain: Lesson 24 practiced whiteboarding a system design under pressure; this wrap-up applies that same discipline to your own finished project.

questions.q: How does this lesson frame the transition into Project 2?
options: Project 2 is a different problem shape (a warehouse migration, not a real-time system), but the retrospective habit and Chapter 1's system-design process carry forward the same way
Project 2 reuses the exact same architecture as Project 1 with no changes
Project 2 has no kickoff or wrap-up lessons of its own
Project 2 does not require applying any system-design process
questions.explain: Lesson 70's kickoff applies the same Chapter 1 process to new constraints, and Lesson 74's wrap-up will ask the same honest retrospective question.
